maria (infra): Quick heads-up — running Q2 capacity signals. Modelled a ~2.2x April peak vs Jan across hosted API. Need decision on how much to commit to reserved GPUs vs short-term leases by EOD Friday.
aj (capacity): Can you share the baseline numbers? reserved vs lease cost delta?
maria (infra): Baseline: cheapest reserved (3yr) saves ~45% vs on-demand, 1yr reserved ~30% savings. But commit risk high if we miss quantized-optim gains. Raw ask: extra 250 A100-equivalent GPU‑hours/sec? sorry, 250 GPUs peak for 3 weeks in April if we don't autoscale aggressively.
jonah (runtime): Clarify: that peak is concurrent requested GPUs, or sustained throughput? Our continuous batching reduces per-token use — if we enable 0.75s latency SLO we can shave ~12% GPU time with batching+cache.
maria (infra): Good point — the model assumed current batching. The 250 is concurrent provisioned GPUs to hit target 95th pct latency at current model mix. If we lower SLO or accept slightly higher tail, capacity drops to ~190 GPUs.
caroline (finance): From cost side — committing to 250 GPUs reserved for Q2 would increase capex/commit by ~$1.1M for the quarter vs leases. But leases (30-90d) push margin pressure and higher unit cost. We have room in operating budget but need leadership OK for the commit delta.
aj (capacity): Proposal: hybrid tiering: reserve 140 GPUs in us-west-2 (where traffic is highest), lease 80 GPUs in eu-west-1 for expected regional spikes, and enable burst pool of 30 GPUs across AZs for canary/failover. That reduces commit and regional risk.
samir (eng-ops): eu-west-1 lease availability is flaky in April per vendor early calendar. If we rely on leases there, plan B should include routing to us-west-2 or us-east-1. Networking: cross-region egress will add ~2-3ms p99 and ~$0.02/token for large responses due to replication + KV syncs.
jonah (runtime): We can deploy a lightweight regional replica with smaller models for EU overflow (reduce fidelity, automatic fallback). That preserves latency SLO and reduces GPU hour demand by ~35% for overflow traffic. Needs rollout window of 2 weeks to test model parity.
aj (capacity): Running numbers: hybrid plan (140 reserved + 80 lease + 30 burst) -> expected cost delta +$650k for the quarter vs base. Full reserve 250 -> +$1.05M. Full lease 250 -> +$1.25M.
caroline (finance): Current risk tolerance: we can approve up to +$700k without exec sign-off. Anything above needs CFO review. So hybrid fits.
infra-bot: [cluster-health] Alert: fleet utilization at 92% in us-west-2 (last 15m), queue delay spiking to 420ms for 99th pct.
maria (infra): infra-bot noted. That's why we want the reserve. Also need plan for autoscale cooldown tuning — current cooldown 6m too long during bursts. Recommend lowering to 90s and enabling pre-warming based on rolling historical signal.
jonah (runtime): Agree: change autoscale cooldown to 90s on the hotspot routes and enable predictive prewarm for top 10 routes. I'll draft the config: ```yaml
route: /v1/generate
prewarm: enabled
prewarm_lookback: 12h
prewarm_threshold: 0.6
cooldown: 90s
```
maria (infra): Action items: 1) aj to confirm vendor lease slots and delivery windows by EOD Wed. 2) caroline to provision hybrid budget approval (~$700k). 3) jonah to run prewarm canary in staging and tune cooldown. 4) samir to draft cross-region routing fallback + egress cost estimate. 5) infra to present hybrid plan in ops sync Friday.
aj (capacity): I will ping vendors and post slots. Also will ask about 30-day flex clauses.
caroline (finance): I'll mark provisional budget and flag CFO if numbers exceed.
samir (eng-ops): Will simulate cross-region egress and post numbers + network playbook.
jonah (runtime): I'll schedule a 2-day canary starting Thu morning.
maria (infra): Thanks — if we can lock the hybrid plan this week, procurement + ops can execute before April surge. :thumbsup: 
aj (capacity): +1
caroline (finance): :ok_hand:
infra-bot: [deploy-bot] Canary rollout for prewarm config scheduled at 2024-04-04T09:00:00Z
